chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from his father, from Hammad bin Isa, from Aban bin Uthman, from the one who informed him, that he said: I said to Abu Ja’far, peace be upon him:
Why was it named a pilgrimage? He said: Pilgrimage is success. It is said: Such-a-person performed the pilgrimage, meaning that he achieved success.
ai.seo_question: What is the linguistic and spiritual meaning behind the name 'Hajj' in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Jawad (or al-Sadiq, depending on the specific chain interpretation) elucidates the linguistic root of 'Hajj' as derived from 'Falah', signifying ultimate spiritual success and prosperity. This etymological link underscores the theological purpose of the pilgrimage not merely as a ritual act, but as a means to attain divine favor and salvation, a concept deeply rooted in Shia exegetical tradition.
